title: Smart Parking intermittently fails to register newly parked vehicles
description: From 16 August 2026 09:10 UTC to 09:48 UTC, the ParkSight Smart Parking application intermittently failed to register newly parked vehicles. Customers reported that vehicles entered parking spaces but some spaces continued to appear available in the application. The parking management API remained reachable and the database remained healthy during the incident. The issue was concentrated in the parking-camera-processing service.

evidence.content: The ParkSight parking-camera-processing service receives frames from parking-lot cameras and performs vehicle detection. Pipeline: Camera -> Frame Capture -> Image Preprocessing -> Vehicle Detection -> Occupancy Decision -> Parking API. A failed or corrupted camera frame can prevent vehicle detection for that frame. The API should only receive an occupancy update after successful vehicle detection.

For camera-processing incidents, engineers should verify: 1. Camera frame ingestion 2. Frame corruption/drop rate 3. Object detection inference 4. Model inference latency 5. GPU/CPU utilization 6. API connectivity 7. Database health. If frame ingestion is failing while downstream API and database services remain healthy, investigate the camera ingestion/processing layer first.
Normal camera processing: Frame ingestion success rate >99.5%, Vehicle detection latency <150ms, Camera frame drop rate <0.5%, GPU utilization 40-75%, Parking API latency <200ms, Database CPU <70%.
